## Why

*Proposed.* Owner decision 2026-11-12 (relay session 8d711f67, chat): "if we're using local we should sliver a larger slice to break it down." A local implementer needs a task small enough to finish within its context and time. When the owner runs a slice above size S on a local implementer, ork first has it carved into slivers (rule u6, one or two files each, size S, effort 1), and the local implementer runs the slivers one after another in the parent's worktree (adj 124, S62, `ork run PARENT --slivers`). Recorded decisions: the cloud spec check row carves the slivers and ork files them with no owner confirmation (adj 337, `roles.local-sliver-carver`); every slice above size S is slivered (adj 338, `roles.local-sliver-when`).
